extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via name parameter — Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server — an attacker can execute arbitrary Python code, read environment variables (including SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN), access the internal Docker network, and pivot to other services. [verified: The `name` query parameter (attacker-controlled) is interpolated via f-string into the template source at line 38, then `Template(content).render()` at line 41 evaluates any Jinja2 syntax (e.g. {{7*7}}) with no sanitization, middleware, or validation — classic SSTI leading to RCE.]

Hardcoded Secrets (SUPER_SECRET_NAME and SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN) — Anyone with access to the source code (public repository) obtains the secrets. The hardcoded token is a high-value asset that can be used to impersonate the application or access protected resources. [verified: Both SUPER_SECRET_NAME ('John Ripper') and SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN ('5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n') are hardcoded string literals in app/config.py:13-15 with FIXME comments confirming they should use os.getenv(); load_dotenv() is called but never queried for these values, so they are committed in plaintext and visible to anyone with repository access.]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via name parameter — An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript into the response page, enabling session theft, credential harvesting, or malicious redirection for any user who visits the crafted URL. [verified: Same code path as SSTI: the unsanitized `name` f-stringed into HTML at line 38 is served via `Template(content).render()` with Jinja2 auto-escaping off by default, and no CSP header is set — `<script>` tags pass through unescaped to the browser.]

Debug Mode Enabled in Production (Information Disclosure) — Attackers can trigger errors to obtain stack traces, source code context, environment variables, and framework internals, enabling them to refine further attacks. [verified: `.env_temp` sets `DEBUG=True`, loaded in `config.py:9` and passed to `FastAPI(debug=True)` at line 14; any unhandled exception (e.g. from a malformed SSTI payload) will leak full stack traces, local variables, and source code with no compensating control.]
